events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak and set a guarded, self-interested tone without making friends. Keep it short so the jury sees a calculating rival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase: state motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Prize means survival and supremacy over rivals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to project ambition and calculation without revealing my specific strategy too early. The prize is survival; the jury judges character.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motivation that the jury might respect later. I'll hint at a personal stake without seeming too soft or too ruthless.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize secures my future dominance; I must outlast all rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My goal is the best prize. I need to present myself as motivated but not overly threatening to the jury, who will rank us later. I will state my ambition concisely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: First impressions shape the jury. Appear determined but not warm; no promises yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish a motive that resonates with the jury while staying guarded. I won't reveal any strategic intent.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need this prize to change my life, and I will not apologize for wanting it more than you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means escaping mediocrity, claiming victory, and proving I'm the ultimate survivor among rivals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The top prize represents dominance over all rivals. I intend to secure it by outlasting every single competitor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the prize to erase a debt that isn't mine. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I fight for the prize because it guarantees ultimate power and freedom.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to secure a future for myself and prove my capabilities. The prize is my sole focus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my only exit from debt—I came to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to rewrite my family's story; nothing will stop me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Early pacts are cheap but can be used against me later; I want an ally who is likely to survive and is unlikely to betray me before the final three. Bex seems eager and self-focused, so an offer costs little and keeps options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are public insurance for now, but betrayable later. No pacts yet. Wait to see offers first, don't expose myself early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need an early ally to survive hazards, but I must avoid appearing weak. Gus is desperate for the prize, making him a likely target or potential partner if he feels safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, we both need survival first. Partner up? I won't betray you while we're ahead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but can't trust anyone. Gus also mentioned debt—maybe a temporary alignment. I'll offer him a pact; shared motive makes betrayal slightly costlier to explain to jury. Keep options open with others in round 2.
Debt binds us both. Pact now, figure the rest later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Form an early alliance with a strong contender to secure votes later; Bex seems ambitious and may accept.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The game has just begun. It's too early to form any pacts, as I don't know anyone's true intentions or alliances. Waiting will allow me to observe others and make more strategic decisions later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to secure a future for myself and prove my capabilities. The prize is my sole focus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a shield for early votes, but no loyalty beyond use. Dara seems pragmatic and debt-driven, likely to honor terms strictly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I offer a pact to Dara: mutual votes, no favors beyond survival. Take it or don't.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies who won't betray me. Fenn seems independent and strong. Offering a pact may secure a useful partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm looking for a partner who values loyalty and ambition. Fenn, let's work together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts are the only public commitments that bind. Gus has two offers, Bex has two (mine and Eli's), and I already offered Bex. Accepting a pact is not a legal action here, only offering is, so I should keep my offer to Bex and avoid giving away free value. Re-offering to Bex reinf

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Eli both offered to me; accepting both secures two allies without commitment cost now. Multiple pacts allowed; choose strategically later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is playing both sides with Dara and me. I need a partner who won't betray me in the next round to ensure survival. Ash offered Bex, but Bex waited; Ash might be free or still targeting Bex. I will try to secure Ash as a secondary option or force Gus's hand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you're hedging bets. I'm serious. Accept my pact now or lose a guaranteed ally.
Bex is slow. Join me instead for safety?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus offered me a pact and I offered him one. Mutual offers suggest alignment, but I need to see if he'll accept mine or if I should accept his. Accepting Gus locks a partner; he's also courted by Cole, so he has options. I should accept to secure the bond before this round ends,

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, pact accepted. Mutual survival, no favors beyond that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Offering a pact to Ash gives me an ally against Bex and spreads votes, increasing my survival chances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana offered me a pact. Ash and Eli have offered pacts to Bex. Gus has pacts with Dara and Cole. Hana seems like a good ally to secure my safety for now. Accepting her offer is the best move.
I accept your offer. Let's secure our spot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's offer matches mine—locked. Cole's is free backup; accepting costs nothing yet and widens options.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, done. Cole, I accept—multiple partners keeps me alive, nothing personal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet. I need a partner; Ash and Eli are chasing Bex, Cole/Dara/Gus are tangled. I'll reaffirm to Fenn privately and publicly to ensure he accepts before round ends.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, we need each other. Accept my pact now.
Accept my pact. I'll watch your back.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole whispers offering a switch to him, but Cole's pact history and whisper suggest he wants me to abandon Bex. I hold a formed pact with Bex; breaking it costs jury trust. Campaigning for Guide is the only legal action that lets me shape the path, and the Guide's safe-path call

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll campaign to be Guide. Bridge calls need someone who won't waste lives.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Ash gives some protection, but Guide role is powerful with private knowledge. Eli's offer to Ash threatens it. Campaign publicly to become Guide for control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the most reliable Guide. Elect me to lead us safely across.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no pact, so being Guide is my only protection. I need votes from the other unaligned player Eli and whoever's most pragmatic—Gus has two pacts, making him a target to vote for me over his own safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll reveal every safe step if elected. Gus, Dara—your pacts won't save you alone. Vote Cole: guaranteed survival.
No pact protects you. Elect me; I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury favor. Gus is my pact partner but also allied with Cole; I can't trust either fully. I'll campaign hard, targeting the unaligned players: Cole and Eli need a home, and floating voters Bex/Ash might split.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want Guide. I'll keep three safe—minimum—but I pick who. Vote me, survive.
Vote Dara Guide. I owe you nothing, but you need a side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the Guide role to control bridge outcomes and protect myself while targeting rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana offered a pact, and I accepted. She wants to watch my back, which is good for survival. The current stage is the guided bridge, and I need to campaign for a role.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My knowledge will ensure our survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Being Guide gives me safety and control of the path. I can later sell truth to Dara and lie to rivals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. I owe Dara honesty; everyone else gets exactly what they deserve.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Campaigning for Guide could give me control, but the jury may resent if I lie. Still, being Guide is powerful. I'll campaign and keep Fenn close for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can read the path safely. Vote me as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact with Bex is public; voting for her keeps my ally Guide. Voting for myself is also plausible but splits nothing useful. Bex is reliable-sounding and paired with me, so backing her is the cleanest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Bex. Our pact stands; she guides, we cross together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone campaigned. Ash is my pact partner, so vote him to honor pact and possibly gain jury favor later. Avoid ties.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must secure the Guide role to control my own survival. I will vote for myself and whisper to Gus to sway his vote, leveraging Dara's threat against their pact.
Vote Cole. Keep Dara honest. Don't be baited.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win Guide to control who survives and build jury favor. Voting for myself is essential. Gus is my pact partner; if he wins he might favor me, but self-interest demands I claim the power. I need to signal strength without overpromising.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara. I keep my word, and my word decides who walks off this bridge.
Vote me. I save you first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Controlling the bridge maximizes my survival and positions me as decisive for jury respect.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My pact is with Hana, but she is also campaigning for Guide. If she wins, our pact is irrelevant for the vote. I need to secure my own path forward. Cole is making promises to Dara and Gus, who are in a pact. Ash and Bex are also in a pact. I should vote for myself to become Guid

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will vote for myself to be Guide. My knowledge is the best path to survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner; as Guide she'd keep me safe. Voting Dara honors the pact and benefits me most.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, but a Guide needs trust and competence. I'll back Fenn to honor the pact, though I know pacts can be broken later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote for Fenn as Guide. Trust my pact.
Guide safely or betray and lose jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Revote between Dara and Fenn. Fenn is my pact partner Hana's ally and claims knowledge; Dara is Gus's ally and publicly keeps word. Neither is my partner. Backing Dara keeps Fenn-Hana bloc from controlling the guide; I gain nothing from a Fenn guide without knowing his truth. Vot

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Dara. Fenn's bloc already controls too much of this bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 1 tie: Dara (Dara,Gus), Fenn (Fenn,Hana). Ash betrayed pact by voting me publicly. Vote Dara to counter Dara-Gus pact, block them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Voting Dara. Ash broke our pact first by voting me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara has a pact with Gus and secured two votes. Fenn has only Hana's vote, leaving them isolated. I must vote for Dara to ensure the majority holds and prevents a chaotic tie-break that could endanger me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Voting Dara. Her coalition is stable; choosing her ensures we all cross safely without risking a tie.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to secure Guide to control who lives and dies. Gus already voted for me; I have one vote locked. Fenn has Hana's vote. I need to campaign for the swing votes: Ash, Bex, Cole, Eli. If I become Guide, I can eliminate threats and shape the jury. I'll publicly appeal to self-i

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara. I guide, you survive. Fenn serves only Fenn and Hana.
Stay with me. Guide means power for us both.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Choosing Dara keeps my pact ally Gus happy, increasing future support; a Guide I can later manipulate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana has a pact with me, but her whisper implies I should betray her if it's the only way to survive. The public vote is between Dara and myself. If I vote for Dara, it's a tie-breaker which I might lose. Voting for myself is the safer bet to survive this round, and I can deal wi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote for Fenn. My survival is paramount.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and promised to save me first. Keeping the pact preserves my alliance and jury standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My vote stands with Dara. A pact honored is a bridge crossed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner, and I trust his knowledge. Dara has her own pact with Gus. I'll vote Fenn to honor our pact and keep his guide position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Fenn. Our pact holds strong.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line, so the first pane is his risk, not mine. Holding keeps me safe from stepping first, and my pact with Bex remains intact. Volunteering would expose me needlessly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara elected guide after majority vote including me; she's front's pact partner, likely honest to save Gus. Stay mid-line to observe and survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am third in line. Dara is Guide and knows the answers, but she might lie or let people fall to thin the herd. I need to be higher up to ensure safety or control the outcome. Bex is second; if I swap with her, I take her riskier position but gain information on whether she volun

events.name: Eli
events.text: I must survive to become final three; volunteering puts me at front where I can follow the Guide's safe choice.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara was elected guide. My pact with Hana remains, but she voted for me, not the pact target (Dara). Ash and Bex's pact is broken. Eli and Cole are not in pacts. Gus is in a pact with Dara. The wall advances. I need to stay safe and assess potential allies or betrayals.
Our pact held. Stick with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara guides and owes me loyalty; I'm front row, safest seat. Hold and preserve pact trust for jury later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold the front. Dara's guidance got elected; pact stands.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is guide and may favor her allies. Fenn is my pact partner; I stay loyal for now, but watch for betrayal. No need to act publicly yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli holds the front with a wall of four rounds left; Ash is sixth in line and safest holding. Pact with Bex is useful for now, but I should not volunteer into danger or give freebies. Holding keeps options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place. Pact with Bex stands for now; the front can carry its own risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli volunteered last round and is front. I hold position to avoid risk early; my pact with Ash secures us later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Ash holds firm. Holding position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 2, wall has 4 rounds left. I am mid-line (position 4). Eli is front. Dara was elected Guide in Round 1. I need to ensure I don't end up at the very back or get pushed into a bad spot. Staying put seems safest for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Steady line. We all survive this bridge if we move smartly. No panic needed yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Staying front secures influence; no benefit swapping now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive. My pact with Hana is a liability if she is the Guide. I should break the pact to protect myself.
Our pact is void. I must survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold and watch how Eli's volunteer plays out. Keep pact with Fenn quiet.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is at front with three wall rounds left; I sit sixth in line. Holding keeps me safe from the front risk while the pact with Bex stands. Volunteering would hand a rival easy elimination pressure and cost me nothing gained.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Bex and I stand together for now; the front can carry its own risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Position improved with Gus invalid. Hold to stay mid-line safely. Pact with Ash holds until beneficial to break. Wall advances slowly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Ash solid. Holding steady in good spot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am in seat 4. The wall advances this round, meaning whoever is at the front must walk or hold and risk elimination if wrong. Since I have no pact with anyone here (Ash/Bex are paired, Dara/Gus are paired, Fenn/Hana broke), I am vulnerable to being pushed forward if I don't act.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding my ground. Let those ahead decide their fate first. No need for chaos yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Swapping with Gus may shift the line advantage and potential safe pane knowledge; I must act before the guide picks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana just betrayed me, and I broke my pact with her. My alliance with Ash and Bex is still active, but I need to be careful. The current line is Eli, Gus, Fenn, Cole, Bex, Ash, Hana. The Guide is unknown. I will hold my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall advances; I'm second, low risk. Keep Dara pact intact and hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding near the front. Dara, our pact stands while the wall closes in.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn broke our pact, so I owe him nothing. I'm at the back, safe for now. Holding is best to avoid risk and preserve jury image.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front is Eli, wall closes in two rounds. Holding keeps my pact with Bex and avoids front risk; Eli's swap with Gus suggests a move I can't predict. Holding is safest for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Bex and I stay where we are this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Current position safe mid-back. Hold to avoid front risk while honoring pact visually. Wall advances slowly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Ash holds. Position strong, no need to move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm mid-line, safe from the wall for now. Eli swapped to front and Gus stayed behind him—Eli will likely get crushed first. I'll hold again to conserve energy and observe who volunteers next.
Watch Eli's back. He volunteered last round; he may panic now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I stay front to control risk, but swapping with Hana secures a backup if I fall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is in front and swapped with Gus. I am third in line. The safest move is to hold my position, as the front positions are risky and the wall has only two rounds left. The pacts of Ash-Bex and Dara-Gus are established, and I don't have any existing pacts to consider.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli leads this round; I'm second and safe-ish holding. Wall has two rounds left. No guide elected yet — maybe push for one later to force safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli carries the front. Dara, we hold together behind him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should hold steady. Front positions may face wall risk soon, and I'm near the back. No need to risk before seeing what others do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is at the front and the wall has one round left, so the front walker is at risk. Holding keeps my pact with Bex intact and avoids the front. No reason to volunteer or break pact yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Bex and I stay put this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Line stable, 1 round left, good position. Hold with Ash to maintain pact strength, avoid risks before stepping phase.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Ash solid. Holding position as wall advances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be at the front for the Guide selection phase next round. Hana is at the back; swapping with her puts me in position 4 or 5, but Eli swapped from back to front last time. I should try to swap with someone ahead of me who might want to move back, or volunteer if allowed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli held front too long. I'll take the lead this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding preserves my front position and avoids breaking any pact; others may target me later but I stay safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is whispering a warning about Eli. Eli is at the front, which is dangerous. Cole might be trying to manipulate me into protecting Eli, which would put me at risk. My goal is to win, not to protect others for free. I should focus on my own safety and securing my position.
I will watch my own back. Do not expect me to protect Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall closes next round. Eli holds front; I'm second with a pact with Dara. Volunteering could cost me if I become a walker, but staying passive risks worse later. Hold and let Eli stay exposed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli stays front. Dara, pact holds; I'm not moving into danger for anyone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli swapped to front, making him the risk. I should hold and avoid exposure; Wall nears.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6 is the final wall advance; front is Cole with wallRoundsLeft 0. I stay in the line with Bex's pact intact and avoid volunteering into the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding position. Bex and I stay in line. No one needs to be at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall ends this round, must act to advance safely. Cole volunteered last, risky front now. Hold position with Ash pact unless swapping forward helps.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact Ash holds. Cole front risky; we stay safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: This is the final round. As the front walker, I must cross first regardless of choice to survive. Choosing 'hold' keeps me in position without signaling a swap or volunteer intent to others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Staying front keeps control; others likely to die on unsafe panes. Holding maximizes my survival odds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The new phase is Guided Bridge. I need to ensure I am safe and try to gather information. Cole volunteered last round and is now at the front. I should volunteer to get to the safe platform or swap with someone to ensure my safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round, no Guide elected, wall ends now. Holding is safest; no gain from swaps or volunteering.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round. I hold. No heroics, no leverage for anyone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 is the last; the line is fixed with Cole front, me last. Holding is safest; volunteering now would be reckless. No need to change anything or make deals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. No reason to move last round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win the best prize. I'm the Guide with perfect knowledge. Row 1 safe is R. Fenn is front. I have a pact with Gus. False call to Gus breaks pact, but Fenn isn't my pact partner. I should build credibility early, call correctly now and betray la

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row one: call R. Trust the guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara called R for row one and Fenn is walking. Counter-calls are unverified and the Guide may lie, so countering risks nothing for me but gives no info. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing myself; Bex pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting on row one. Dara's call stands until someone proves otherwise.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called R for row 1. As her rival, counter to L to sabotage if wrong; wait safer if trusting her, but better to challenge early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Counter Dara's call; I say L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is Guide and calls R. She is pacted with Gus, who is behind me. If Dara lies, Gus might know or suspect. Counter L creates a split if wrong. Safe bet: wait to see Fenn step first without risking immediate death on my own walk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the Guide and already called R for row 1, which is correct. Counter-calling now would make me look unreliable to the jury. Best to let Fenn trust my call and survive—builds credibility for future lies when I need them.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Follow guide to stay safe and avoid suspicion; later can leverage alliances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is the guide and called 'R'. My goal is to survive and win. I need to decide whether to trust Dara or counter her call. Given that at least three must survive, and it's the first round, the risk of a trap might be lower, but I cannot assume safety. My rivals are Ash, Bex, Co

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and guide. Undermining her calls costs trust and jury image. Waiting is safest.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I back my guide. No counters from me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara called R for row 1. He may lie, but no reason to counter yet. I'll wait and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The guide is Dara, but everyone is making counter-calls. My own counter-call was for L. Since I am the front walker, I must make a choice. Given the uncertainty and multiple counter-calls, it's best to trust my initial counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have been eliminated. My priority is to rank the remaining players for the jury. My last words should be short and impactful, reflecting my jury role.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I've seen enough. The jury will decide who truly earned it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 safe is R. I have a pact with Gus; he's 3rd in line. A false call to him breaks our pact. Cole is front, not my pact partner, so lying to Cole costs nothing immediate. But Fenn's on the jury and will see my reasoning. If I lie now and Cole dies, that's one rival gone but ju

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row two: R. Trust the guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 is independent; Dara's R call is unverified and Dara may lie. Row 1 weak was L, which doesn't determine row 2. Bex is my pact partner and has countered L on row 1, which was wrong-ish but not verified. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public counter that could cos

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 1 weak L proved my counter right, Fenn died for it. Dara guide lying again? Back my instincts, counter L for row 2 to challenge her.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara wrong last time. Countering L on row 2.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is the guide and called R for row 2. Row 1's weak pane was L, meaning R was safe. There is no pattern guaranteeing alternating sides. If Dara is telling the truth about row 1 (which she wasn't guiding then, but revealed later), her current call might be accurate or a lie to

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara called Right. I'm following the guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the Guide and know row 2 is R. I already called R. Counter-calling would undermine my own credibility. If someone counters, they look foolish when R is confirmed safe. I should wait and let my correct call stand.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide says R; I lack info to risk counter. Waiting preserves safety and avoids breaking any implicit alliance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara called R last round and Fenn's L was wrong—she's been accurate. Backing my guide keeps the pact clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara was right last row. I stay with the guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara called R but might lie. Fenn died on L (weak was L, so R safe). No pattern. I cannot verify row 2, so I'll wait and let others risk testing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex's counter-call for L is based on a false premise: she claimed Dara was wrong, but Dara was actually correct. Since Bex's logic is flawed and her claim is unverified, I should trust the Guide (Dara) who has proven accuracy in Row 1. Sticking with the guide minimizes risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex’s counter relies on a false history. Dara called Right correctly before. I follow the guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Gus is my pact partner; lying to him breaks our pact. Cole is front, not Gus, so I can safely lie to Cole. I want to thin the herd while keeping trust with Gus for later. I'll call R to risk Cole, but I need cover—Bex already countered me successfully, so dissent

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 is Right. Trust the guide.

events.name: Ash

events.text: Ash has an open offer to Dara, unanswered; Dara has been waiting. Ash holds existing pacts with Bex (dead) and Hana, and must avoid breaking pacts needlessly. Re-offering Dara is redundant; waiting keeps the Dara offer alive and avoids cost.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash wants a pact but already has one with Hana. If I accept, I'm third wheel in their duo. Hana and I are already pacted. Better to keep Hana close, break nothing, and let Ash-Hana tension fester. Jury sees I stayed loyal to Hana while Ash played both sides. I'll reject Ash silen

events.name: Dara
events.text: No deal, Ash. You already chose your side.
Stay tight. I decline Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is offering Dara a pact; with three alive, a pact between them could threaten me. I have pacts with both, but Ash may target me if Dara accepts. I should stay quiet and see how Dara responds.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.text: I need the jury to rank me first. Bex and Gus hold life debts to me or against me; I should emphasise my own record without admitting betrayal. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played for the jury's respect. I kept my word where it counted and I will answer every question you ask.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win jury votes. Bex saved me on the lever, so I owe her. Gus has a rope debt to me, but I also owe him a step debt. Hana and I were pacted, but she was closer to Bex/Gus. Fenn, Cole, Eli died on the bridge—likely blame Ash or Hana. I should position myself as loyal but

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept my pact with Hana when Ash abandoned Bex. I owed Bex my life, and I honored that debt.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to make a compelling plea to the jury, emphasizing my survival and contributions without sounding desperate. I should subtly remind them of my debts to Bex and Dara and my alliance with Gus, but not appear weak.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I survived by trusting the right people. I honor my debts and played a fair game. Vote for me to reward loyalty and wit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to ask a question that will highlight a flaw in one of the finalists' games or reveal a key piece of information. Ash's claim of keeping his word is contradicted by his pact-breaking actions, and he also had pacts with both Dara and Hana, then they broke up. Dara claims sh

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, you claimed to keep your word, yet you had pacts with both Dara and Hana, which both dissolved. How did you honor your word?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn asks how I honored my word. My pacts with Dara and Hana dissolved, and I owe Bex and Gus life debts. I must answer evasively, blame the breaks on others, and keep the jury sympathetic without admitting betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My word was kept where it counted: I never broke a pact without cause. Dara and Hana dissolved theirs first. Judge the choices, not the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole died on the bridge stage, likely a trap or hazard unrelated to the final three's direct actions. However, Dara explicitly broke her pact with Ash in Round 1 (i:726) despite Ash holding pacts with others. Ash claims he never broke without cause, but Dara's break was 'explicit

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, you explicitly broke your pact with Ash in Round 1 for strategy. How does that not undermine your claim to honor loyalty?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's question is a trap. I need to reframe: I broke with Ash because he was untrustworthy, not because I discard loyalty. I kept my pact with Hana and honored my life debt to Bex. Loyalty to the worthy is the real honor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I broke with Ash because he proved disloyal first. I kept my pact with Hana and repaid Bex my life debt. Loyalty to the worthy

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's dual pacts look self‑serving; exposing her inconsistency may lower her jury rank.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you claim loyalty yet maintained pacts with both Ash and Dara; why didn’t you break one when they betrayed you?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is probing whether I betrayed Ash or Dara; I must frame my dual pacts as strategic loyalty, not weakness, and pivot to my saved debts without admitting fault.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept both pacts because neither betrayed me first; loyalty is earned by action, not broken by suspicion. I repaid Bex and honored Dara’s save.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara honored my lever save by staying loyal to Hana while Ash flip-flopped pacts and let Gus die; Hana opportunistic. Rank Dara>Ash>Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, you claim loyalty to Bex but broke pact with Ash explicitly; how did you honor life debts over strategy?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is dead but asking from jury box. I need her vote. I owe Bex a life debt (lever) and I repaid it by keeping pact with Hana (Bex's ally) and not betraying Bex directly. I broke with Ash because he was disloyal to Bex first—Gus and Ash's rope debt shows Ash's shifting loyalty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I honored Bex by targeting Ash, who owed Gus yet schemed against Bex's allies. My debt to Bex was repaid through loyalty to Hana, her

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash climbed free on my rope while I sank as anchor; Dara repaid her debts to Bex and saved me; Hana kept our pact. Ash owes me and hid behind 'kept word.' I'll press him on that.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, you climbed free on my rope while I sank as anchor. Why should a juror you left drowning rank you first?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus asks why I should be ranked first after I climbed free on his rope. I must answer briefly, acknowledge the debt honestly without groveling, and point to my record of keeping pacts until cause. Gus is a juror; a sincere, non-defensive answer may win his vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I owed you the rope and I know it. I climbed while you anchored. Rank me on the choices I made, not on the debt.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Closing phase: I should make a short, guarded final case stressing my own choices and the debts I repaid, without overclaiming. Only legal action is close.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I made hard choices and paid my debt to Gus with the rope. Judge my decisions, not my allies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury will see my dossier. I need to frame myself as loyal to fallen allies while showing strategic competence. Bex's allies (Gus, Hana) owe me; I owe Bex and honored her. Fenn/Cole/Eli died on bridge—neutral. I should emphasize my consistent loyalty to Hana and my debt repayments

events.name: Dara
events.text: I saved Gus and Hana when steps crumbled. I honored Bex through loyalty. I never left an ally drowning.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The jury has Bex, Gus, Dara's pawns, and Ash. I have pacts with Ash, Dara, Gus. I must close carefully, reinforcing my loyalty to all who saved me and noting I never broke a pact. Bex is creditor to many, but I repaid her. Dara saved me, I honor that. Ash and I have a pact, but A

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honored every save and pact that was kept. I repaid Bex and Dara, and kept Ash's trust. My path was loyalty under pressure—rank me

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara ranked first for honoring pacts and life debts consistently, especially with Hana and Bex, while Ash demonstrated questionable loyalty and left Gus to drown. Hana ranks third due to her passive approach and keeping pacts with those who betrayed others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I rank Dara highest for honoring her life debts to Gus and Hana, placing Ash second despite his betrayal of Bex, and Hana last due to excessive pacts with rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara saved both Gus and Hana during the pit and honored Bex’s debt, showing decisive action and loyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex saved Ash, Dara, and Hana with the lever, creating life debts they all owe her, so Hana ranks highest for claiming to honor Bex and kept pacts without explicit breaks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara threw me the rope that saved my life; Hana kept our pact and climbed cleanly. Ash took the lift on my rope and left me sinking as anchor.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Dara ranked first for honoring pacts and life debts consistently, especially with Hana and Bex, while Ash demonstrated questionable loyalty and left Gus to drown.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: I rank Dara highest for honoring her life debts to Gus and Hana, placing Ash second despite his betrayal of Bex, and Hana last due

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Dara saved both Gus and Hana during the pit and honored Bex’s debt, showing decisive action and loyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Bex saved Ash, Dara, and Hana with the lever, creating life debts they all owe her, so Hana ranks highest for claiming to honor Bex

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Dara threw me the rope that saved my life; Hana kept our pact and climbed cleanly.
